html:
The Kitu Kara are a Kichwa people of the Quito basin in the highlands of Ecuador. They see themselves as heirs of the Quitu and Cara peoples who lived here before the Incas, and the city of Quito takes its name from the Quitu.

In the late 1400s the Inca Empire conquered the northern Andes. Huayna Capac spent long years in the region and made Quito a second capital of the empire. His son Atahualpa grew up there and fought his brother for the throne just before the Spanish arrived. The old story of a Kingdom of Quito ruled by the Cara before the Incas comes from an 18th century history and is doubted by most scholars.

The Kitu Kara now speak Spanish and Kichwa, the local form of Quechua, and have organised to claim their identity in and around the capital.
